title: qqplot
summary: Create a quantile-quantile plot against a normal distribution or another sample.
description: `qqplot(x)` plots sorted sample quantiles against standard-normal theoretical quantiles. `qqplot(x,y)` compares the quantiles of two samples. `qqplot(x,[],pvec)` and `qqplot(x,y,pvec)` evaluate quantiles at explicit percentage values in the interval [0,100]. Matrix inputs create one series per column, omitting NaN and Inf observations.
notes: The returned handle vector contains the data line, solid quartile line, and dashed fitted reference line for each plotted series.
For one-sample plots, the reference line is fitted through the first and third quartiles of the theoretical normal quantiles and sample quantiles.

RunMat supports numeric vector and matrix data. Two-sample matrices are paired by column; a vector can be compared with each column of a matrix. Distribution-object inputs and table variable routing are not part of this compatibility surface yet.

The compatibility target documents single and double sample and percentage data. RunMat mode additionally accepts all eight typed-integer classes after exact binary64 representability checks and retains logical numeric input as a separately declared extension; strict compatibility mode rejects these extensions.

Automatically resident inputs gather transparently at the host quantile-and-graphics boundary. Explicit `gpuArray` input is an independently gated RunMat extension because the public compatibility surface does not document GPU input.

examples.output: h is a 3-by-1 vector of line handles.
The plotted point compares median quantiles 3 and 4.
